patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hive and Jira share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Hive only if your buying job matches “Work management platform with free plan (≤10 members) and Teams from $12/user/mo annual — ” rather than Jira's shape. Choose Jira only if your buying job matches “Atlassian Agile issue tracker for software teams — Free ≤10; Standard from ~$8.15/user/mo ” rather than Hive's shape. Workflow advantage: Hive leans team-collaboration-work; Jira leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hive and Jira share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Hive is Work management platform with free plan (≤10 members) and Teams from $12/user/mo annual — strong monday.com peer.; Jira is Atlassian Agile issue tracker for software teams — Free ≤10; Standard from ~$8.15/user/mo annual..
- Company-size focus: Hive (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs Jira (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Hive-leaning team-collaboration-work vs Jira-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Hive — Free and Starter cap members/projects at 10 — growth forces Teams; Jira — Steep learning curve outside engineering.

Limitations — Hive: Free and Starter cap members/projects at 10 — growth forces Teams; Free storage (200MB) and AI credits (1k) are tight for active teams; Jira: Steep learning curve outside engineering; Confluence often required for wiki/docs depth.

Poor-fit cases: Hive is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Free and Starter cap members/projects at 10 — growth forces Teams · Jira is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Steep learning curve outside engineering · Avoid Hive if you actually need Jira's motion (Atlassian Agile issue tracker for software teams — Free ≤10; Standard from ~$8.1)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
